info.title: Markers in descriptions — demo file
info.description: A contract in the shape it leaves the EA generator in: everything the generator cannot express sits in the descriptions as [field: value] markers. Text values — texts, dates, identifiers, enum values — are written in quotes, just like in JSON; numbers, flags and booleans without. Run the "OpenAPI: Apply Markers" command and compare it with the README. Once the file is saved the markers are gone from the descriptions — `npm run demo:reset` brings back a copy to play with again.

post.description: Registers a new measurement station. Markers are read from BOTH fields: consumes/produces sit higher up in summary, the rest here. Named example cases need OpenAPI 3.x, so on this 2.0 file all three of them wait in the description until the contract is converted. Every part of a case is a marker of its own, so nothing needs quoting and the parts may stand in any order. [order:] decides where a case lands in the Swagger UI dropdown, [required] builds the smallest body the contract accepts, and a case with no [exampleBody:] is composed from the [example:] markers on the fields of Station, so a field added later needs no example rewritten by hand. [operationId: "createStation"] [tags: "Stations", "Sensors"] [x-audit: {"level":"high"}] [requestCase: [name: minimal] [summary: The smallest body the contract accepts] [order: 1] [required]] [requestCase: [name: standard] [summary: Standard registration — values from the model] [order: 2]] [requestCase: [name: maintenance] [summary: Station taken in for maintenance] [order: 3] [exampleBody: {"serial": "ST/2026/000999", "status": "MAINTENANCE"}]] [TODO: write down the daily reading limits]

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The channel the request came in through. [enum: "WEB", "MOBILE", "API"] [example: "WEB"] [default: "WEB"]

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items to return — numbers without quotes. [minimum: 1] [maximum: 100] [multipleOf: 5] [default: 20]

parameters.name: methods
parameters.description: Alert channels — a list on an array parameter. [example: ["SMS", "MAIL"]] [uniqueItems] [minItems: 1] [maxItems: 5]

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: A free-form operator note — nothing here hints at the content, so an example should NOT show up.

get.description: The old way of reading a station. A summary made up of nothing but a marker has to disappear, not stay as an empty string. [operationId: "getStationLegacy"] [summary: "Read a station (retiring version)"] [tags: "Stations"] [deprecated]

serial.description: Serial number given by the system. [title: "Station serial"] [example: "ST/2026/000123"] [pattern: "^ST/\d{4}/\d{6}$"] [readOnly]

region.description: Region — a pattern on its own gives no example; without a marker the field stays empty. [pattern: "^\d{3}$"]

status.description: Station status — enum and default set from markers; we do NOT make up an example. [enum: "ACTIVE", "MAINTENANCE", "RETIRED"] [default: "ACTIVE"]

stationId.description: Technical identifier — a uid in quotes. [format: "uuid"] [example: "3f2504e0-4f89-41d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301"]

installedOn.description: Installation date — a date in quotes. [format: "date"] [example: "2026-03-01"]

createdAt.description: When the record was created — a format on its own gives no example. [format: "date-time"]

mastHeight.description: Mast height in metres — numbers without quotes, with a decimal point, exactly as in the file. [minimum: 0.5] [maximum: 100] [multipleOf: 0.5]

antennas.description: Number of antennas — in Swagger 2.0 exclusiveMinimum is a boolean and has to carry an explicit value (a bare [exclusiveMinimum] with no value stays in the description). [minimum: 0] [exclusiveMinimum: true] [maximum: 4]

code.description: Internal code — the quotes leave the leading zero alone. [example: "0012"] [minLength: 4] [maxLength: 4]

items.description: Available ways of announcing failed readings [example: ["SMS", "MAIL"]]

failedReadingAlertMethods.description: A 0..* attribute — EA sticks the note on the ELEMENT TYPE, and the list still has to land on the array.

channels.description: The same list, but with the note written on the array. [example: ["WEB", "MOBILE"]] [minItems: 1] [uniqueItems]

singleChannel.description: A single value written on the array — the result has to be a one-element list. [example: "SMS"]

items.description: An example of a SINGLE value stays on the element. [example: "SMS"]
A list of numbers from the element note — numbers without quotes. [example: [10, 20, 30]]
The element is a shared type — the list lands on the array and the type itself is left untouched. [example: ["AB", "CD"]]
A list of lists — here the array of values belongs to the element, because the element IS itself an array. [example: [1, 2]]
The list goes to the array, while the pattern describes the element and stays on it (the element has no example of its own). [example: ["AB"]] [pattern: "^[A-Z]{2}$"]

unknownValue.description: An explicit absence of a value — null WITHOUT quotes, because it is not a text. [example: null]

literalNull.description: A literal four-letter text — in quotes, so it is an ordinary string. [example: "null"]

quotedSpecialChars.description: Quotes protect the square bracket, the comma and the spaces at the edges of the value. [example: "a]b, c"]

items.description: A comma inside quotes belongs to the value, it does not split the list. [example: ["A,B", "C"]]

unquotedStillWorks.description: Quotes are not required — it works without them too, you just cannot see where the value ends. [example: no remarks]

optionalRemark.description: A field that may arrive empty. [nullable] [example: "no remarks"]

unsupportedPattern.description: A pattern that cannot be reversed easily — we generate nothing from it anyway. [pattern: "^(?!bad)ok$"]

altitude.description: Altitude above sea level — a pattern applies ONLY to strings, so on a numeric field the marker stays in the description instead of soaking into the file as a dead entry. [pattern: "^\d+\.\d{2}$"] [example: 1250.00]

altitudeAsText.description: The same altitude modelled as a text — only here does the pattern make sense, and the quotes keep the trailing zeros. [pattern: "^\d+\.\d{2}$"] [example: "1250.00"]

quotedOnNumber.description: Quotes on a numeric field do not match the type — the marker stays in the description instead of putting a text where the contract promises a number. [example: "1250.00"]

commaDecimal.description: A decimal comma is not how numbers are written in this file — the marker stays in the description. [example: 0,5]

boolWord.description: On a boolean field only true/false fits — a word in any language stays in the description. [example: yes]

flagTypo.description: A typo in a flag value does not switch it on quietly. [readOnly: fasle]

doubledBackslashes.description: WITHOUT quotes the content is taken literally, so \\d means "a backslash, then the letter d" and matches nothing — the field ends up on the "example does not match the pattern" list. [pattern: ^\\d+$] [example: "12345"]

quotedBackslashes.description: The same text IN QUOTES reads like it would in JSON: \\d is one backslash and the letter d, that is a valid pattern for digits. [pattern: "^\\d+$"] [example: "12345"]

misplacedConstraint.description: A numeric constraint on a text — that stays in the description too. [minimum: 1]

freeText.description: A text with no marker — it is left without an example.

boundedText.description: Length limits from markers; no example. [minLength: 5] [maxLength: 10]

counter.description: A number with no marker — no example.

heatedEnclosure.description: A boolean with no marker — no example.

autoCalibration.description: A boolean with a default value — true/false, without quotes. [default: false]

notTouched.description: Markers outside the dictionary stay in the description where a human can see them: [0..1] [TODO: agree with the data team] [frmat: uuid] — a typo in the key is not guessed at.

sharedType.description: A type from the shared model that must not be touched — the note sits ONE LEVEL UP, on the field. A value next to a bare $ref would be ignored in both 2.0 and 3.0, so the field gets wrapped in a one-element allOf. [example: "AB"]

sharedTypeNoMarker.description: The same field without a marker of its own — it stays a bare reference and shows the shared type's example.

spreadOperator.description: [exampleBody:] spreads a ready-made piece of the payload ACROSS THE FIELDS — every field gets its own example, instead of one big example on top. [exampleBody: {"firstName": "Alex", "lastName": "Meyer", "unit": "hPa"}]

Operator.description: Operator details — no markers, so no examples: what to show is up to Swagger UI.

email.description: E-mail address — format and pattern from markers, no example. [format: "email"] [pattern: "^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[a-z]{2,}$"]

postalCode.description: Postal code — the pattern alone, no example. [pattern: "^\d{2}-\d{3}$"]

Code.description: A shared type from the common model. Its example (from a marker) applies everywhere a field has none of its own. [example: "ZZ"]

message.description: A message for the caller — a comma and a full stop inside the value are safe in quotes. [example: "The station serial does not match the pattern, correct the data."]
